answer: Drip-timing enrollment gate: identities must perform their first action within a randomized window whose start is published by a periodic network beacon. The rule rejects any batch of registrations whose inter-arrival spacing matches the beacon cadence too closely, since a single operator replaying one clock produces a flat dune of simultaneous arrivals. Honest clients add jitter sourced from local entropy, so a mass producer must run separate timing infrastructure per identity, raising per-identity cost by a fresh clock and proxy, timber by timber.
